Class BenchmarkComparison

java.lang.Object
grafioschtrader.reportviews.performance.BenchmarkComparison
public final class BenchmarkComparison extends Object
Compares the time-weighted series of a report with an aligned benchmark over common intervals. A pure function of its two inputs, fixed by hand-calculated tests.

The common intervals J are the intervals i of the comparison span (k, e] in which the portfolio has a usable capital base. For a base index f >= k and an end index t <= e: 

portfolioReturn(f, t) = product over i in J, f < i <= t of g_i - 1
benchmarkReturn(f, t) = product over i in J, f < i <= t of (b_i / b_(i-1)) - 1

Both are null when no interval of J lies in (f, t]. Inside the span the portfolio side equals ReturnSeries.linked(int, int), which already skips unusable intervals. An interval without portfolio capital is skipped on both sides, so neither earns anything in such a gap.

    • metrics

      public BenchmarkMetrics metrics(long minAnnualizationDays, Function<LocalDate, Double> annualRate)
      The figures of the whole span, including the relative risk of BenchmarkRisk. Annualized returns need the given number of calendar days and no gap in the exposure, otherwise a gap would be scaled as if it had been invested.
      Parameters:
      minAnnualizationDays - fewest calendar days from which returns are annualized: 360 for the report, 0 for the replay
      annualRate - the annual risk-free rate of the main currency known on a date; null without rates
      Returns:
      the metrics, null without a span

    • chart

      public List<BenchmarkChartPoint> chart(Double[] shadowValues)
      One chart point per valuation date. At the first date of the span both returns are 0; later dates carry the returns linked from it. Dates outside the span and intervals without portfolio capital give null returns. Inside the span every point carries the value of the portfolio and that of the shadow portfolio.
      Parameters:
      shadowValues - values of the shadow portfolio per valuation date, null where it has none
      Returns:
      the points in the order of the valuation dates
